frontier.hypothesis: The residual is not in the blend arm's SPELLING but in its block STRUCTURE or the surrounding chassis - the `if (i == count - 1)` split, the `px == 0` early-out, the `goto loop_check` exits, the declaration scope of the arm's locals relative to the two enclosing blocks, and the outer per-row block's contents were all held fixed by this sweep.
frontier.mechanism: 1,496 exhaustive spellings of the arm and 20 of the latch all bottom at 12 with the identical 12 rows, so every axis the generator varies is exhausted; the only remaining C-level degrees of freedom in the region are structural.
frontier.next_probe: Move the head/tail split in tmp/grind/func_8003DE14/s25/gen.py outward one block (head ends before the `if (i == count - 1)` test), add axes for the early-out shape and for declaration scope, regenerate and re-sweep with tools/sweep_variants.py; ~1.8 s per body, so a 1,000-body space is ~30 minutes.

frontier.hypothesis: The two FREE axes at the floor are the cheapest place to introduce an extra pseudo without paying, which is exactly what s24 frontier item 2 (change reg 138's nrefs/livelen without naming it) needs.
frontier.mechanism: A fresh `bp` for the blue complement product and a fresh named red sum each hold the floor at 12/173, so an added ordinary-C use sited there does not trigger the collateral re-seating that killed every earlier nrefs/livelen attempt.
frontier.next_probe: Starting from v1442 (both free axes taken), sweep ordinary-C shapes that consume the blue sum one statement later or give the blue channel an extra use of an already-live value, reading the BB2_ALLOC_DEBUG ord/pri row for pseudo 138 on each form that scores <= 12.

frontier.hypothesis: s24 frontier item 1 is still un-run: the sum-to-operand tie is either local-alloc's combine_regs or merely find_free_reg's scan order, and the two imply different levers.
frontier.mechanism: s24's c1 result (a carrier dying in two places did NOT untie the red add) argues against combine_regs (tools/gcc-2.7.2/local-alloc.c:1784); if the sum and its operand merely got the same hard register by first-fit, the lever is the quantity ORDER (qty_compare), not any death count, and every death-count lever tried in s23/s24 aimed at the wrong predicate.
frontier.next_probe: Re-run tmp/grind/func_8003DE14/s24/alloc.sh with BB2_QTY_DEBUG=1 BB2_SUGG_DEBUG=1 on the p2 body and map block-10 qty18/reg152, qty16/reg132, qty17/reg149, qty15/reg131 onto the red sum, the green sum, rp, gp and px by cross-reading tmp/grind/func_8003DE14/dumps/code6cac_c2.lreg. Same qty => combine_regs; different qty, same hard reg => scan order. Only then spell C.
